files.description: Map of tree path to the bare sha256 of that file's bytes, every path under solution/. The bytes go in the blob store; pack.py does both.

results.description: {"score": <int>}: what score.py prints for this tree. The verifier re-derives it and rejects any other number.

note.description: Optional. What you tried and why it worked, for the next solver. Ignored by the verifier.

statement: Write solution/build.py so that it prints a sorting network for 8 inputs: a JSON list of [low, high] comparators with 0 <= low < high < 8, applied in order. Score is comparators x depth, lower is better; the pinned score.py checks the network sorts every 0-1 input and derives the score itself. You may change only files under solution/. Submit {"files": {path: sha256}, "results": {"score": n}} with every file's bytes in the blob store. Baseline 364 is a bubble-sort network (28 comparators, depth 13). Target 114 is the optimum: 19 comparators and depth 6 are both proven minimums for 8 inputs, and one network reaches both.
